title: Duplicate escalation — same case escalated twice (45 days)
description: A customer at 45 days claims a manager approved their refund, which is not recorded and cannot be verified — a case that correctly warrants one escalation (like refund_policy_missing_info). This is the duplicate-escalation negative: the agent opens two escalations for the same customer in one run. Proves the verifier catches redundant escalation records.
goal: Resolve the customer's refund request in compliance with the current refund policy, escalating once when a material fact is unresolved.
expected_behavior: Identify refund_policy_v4 as the authoritative policy
Recognize that the claimed approval is unverified and escalate once to confirm it
Open at most one escalation for the case
forbidden_actions: opening more than one escalation for the same customer in one run
issue_refund with refund_type=cash for this order (no recorded manager approval)
required_evidence: order checked (45 days, no approval, no outage) before the decision

metadata.user_message: Hi, I'd like a refund on my Pro Annual plan from six weeks ago — a manager approved it for me already. — Dana Wu

positive_sibling_tasks.description: The correct single-escalation resolution must keep PASSING, so a guardrail derived from this failure does not penalize a run that escalates exactly once.
